8 Part A — Data Reduction

Having more data is usually good, but having too many columns (features) can paralyze a machine learning model.

8.1 1. Dimensionality and Numerosity Reduction

Dimensionality reduction is the process of reducing the number of columns in a dataset. Numerosity reduction is reducing the number of rows.

It exists to solve the Curse of Dimensionality. If you are trying to predict the price of a car, using 5 columns (mileage, age, brand, engine size, condition) is great. Using 5,000 columns (including the exact hex code of the paint, the thread count of the seats, the brand of the radio dial) will confuse the model. It will desperately try to find patterns in the noise.

Tip🧠 Analogy — The Shadow

The everyday thing: Looking at a 3D object’s shadow.

The mapping: - A dataset with 3 columns is a 3D object. - PCA (Dimensionality Reduction) shines a light on that object to cast a 2D shadow. - You lose one dimension of detail (depth), but you still retain the overall shape of the object, and a 2D shadow is much easier to draw (process).

8.1.1 How it works

  • Principal Component Analysis (PCA): A mathematical technique that compresses multiple correlated columns into a smaller set of “Principal Components” that capture the majority of the original variance.
  • Data Cube Aggregation: Grouping row data (e.g., combining daily sales into monthly sales to reduce the row count).

8.1.2 ❓ MCQs

Q1. What is the primary goal of Dimensionality Reduction (like PCA)?

    1. To delete all the outliers in a dataset.
    1. To reduce the number of columns while retaining as much of the original information as possible.
    1. To reduce the number of rows by taking a random sample.
NoteAnswers

A1 — (b). PCA mathematically compresses columns. Reducing rows is numerosity reduction (sampling or aggregation).

9 Part B — Discretization

Sometimes specific numbers don’t matter as much as the category they fall into.

9.1 2. Top-down and Bottom-up Discretization

Discretization (Binning) is the process of converting continuous numbers into discrete categories.

It exists because human behavior often reacts to thresholds, not continuous scales. A marketing algorithm doesn’t need to know the difference between a 21-year-old and a 22-year-old. It needs to know if they are a “Young Adult” or a “Senior.”

9.1.1 How it works

  • Top-Down (Splitting): You look at the whole dataset (Ages 0 to 100) and decide to split it into equal chunks: [0-33], [34-66], [67-100].
  • Bottom-Up (Merging): You start with exact numbers (Ages 21, 22, 23) and merge them based on similarity until distinct groups form.

10 Part Demo — PCA and Cut

Using PCA to compress a dataset, and Pandas .cut() to discretize age.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# --- 1. DISCRETIZATION (pd.cut) ---
ages = pd.DataFrame({"Age": [15, 22, 34, 45, 65, 80, 12, 29]})
# Convert continuous ages into buckets!
ages["Age_Group"] = pd.cut(ages["Age"], bins=[0, 18, 35, 60, 100], labels=["Child", "Young Adult", "Adult", "Senior"])

print("--- Discretized Ages ---")
display(ages.head())

# --- 2. PCA (Dimensionality Reduction) ---
# Imagine a dataset with 3 correlated columns: Height, Arm Span, Leg Length
np.random.seed(42)
height = np.random.normal(170, 10, 100)
arm_span = height * 1.02 + np.random.normal(0, 2, 100)
leg_length = height * 0.45 + np.random.normal(0, 1, 100)

df_3d = pd.DataFrame({"Height": height, "Arm_Span": arm_span, "Leg_Length": leg_length})

# Compress these 3 columns into just 1 Principal Component
pca = PCA(n_components=1)
compressed_1d = pca.fit_transform(df_3d)

print(f"\n--- PCA Compression ---")
print(f"Original shape: {df_3d.shape} (3 columns)")
print(f"Compressed shape: {compressed_1d.shape} (1 column)")
print(f"Variance explained by 1 component: {pca.explained_variance_ratio_[0]*100:.2f}%")
# We shrunk the data by 66%, but kept 99% of the information!
--- Discretized Ages ---

--- PCA Compression ---
Original shape: (100, 3) (3 columns)
Compressed shape: (100, 1) (1 column)
Variance explained by 1 component: 98.40%
Warning⚠️ The trap of PCA interpretability

While PCA is amazing for compression, it destroys human interpretability. After running PCA, you no longer have a “Height” column. You have a “Principal Component 1” column, which is a mathematically blended smoothie of Height, Arm Span, and Leg Length.
